function: Beamforming: a liquid neural network (GLNN) outputs a residual update of the compressed precoder base matrix to maximize weighted sum spectral efficiency in mmWave MU-MIMO (p. 2-3).
system: Downlink mmWave MU-MIMO: BS with M=64 antennas, K=4 users with Nk=2 receive antennas each, 28 GHz; no RIS (p. 4).
method: Gradient-based liquid neural network: ODE-based liquid neurons take loss gradients as input; trained with Adam on a rate-based loss, 500-sample warm-up then online updates (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Open-source DeepMIMO dataset, scenario O1, BS3, 28 GHz; channel estimation error modeled as zero-mean white Gaussian; 500 samples with continuously changing positions (p. 4).
test_conditions: Warm-up of 500 samples; results averaged over 500 generated samples with changing positions; sweeps of power and CEE; online run without warm-up at 6, 15, 30 m/s (p. 4-5).
baselines: WMMSE (iterative, non-learned) [20]; LAGD [9] and LSTM (learned); upper bound from 100 runs on perfect CSI (p. 4).
metrics: Spectral efficiency (bps/Hz) versus transmit power, CEE and time slots; CPU time per sample versus number of BS antennas M (p. 4-5).
complexity: Order O(Ne(MNK+M^2K+Nk^3)) per sample, compared with baselines in Table I; CPU time per sample for M=32 to 160, 1.61% of WMMSE at M=160 (p. 5).
openness: Code open source at https://github.com/tp1000d/GLNN (p. 2, ref. [15] on p. 5); DeepMIMO is public (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "We construct the channel matrix using BS3 from scenario O1 of the open source DeepMIMO dataset [19]"
q2_support: p. 4: "We provide three phases of speed, including 6 m/s, 15 m/s, and 30 m/s"; p. 5: "this increased gap swiftly closes as the GLNN adapts after just a few iterations"
q3_support: p. 4: "Baseline 1 (WMMSE): An iterative scheme from [20]."; p. 4: "Baseline 2 (LAGD): A DL-based model from [9]."
q4_support: p. 2: "as low as only 1.61% of the time consumption"; p. 5: "Table I provides a comparison of the computational complexity between GLNN and the baselines"
q5_support: p. 2: "we have made our work open source at [15]"
